subject: Linkage map construction with BC data

messages.author: 6471ff4d3e4b5639
messages.subject: Linkage map construction with BC data
parts:
Hello,

I am attempting to construct a linkage map for 241 backcrossed individuals with a total of 2805 markers. My data initially consisted of many thousand scaffolds with >30,000 positions total. I've collapsed my data set so that the genotype of each column is the mode genotype for a particular scaffold. This was done as I was having issues working with the larger data set.

Generally following the steps of the genetic maps tutorial (I've already gotten rid of poor markers below), I generate my linkage maps with:

mapthis<-read.cross("csv",file="test.csv", crosstype='bc',estimate.map=FALSE)
mapthis <- est.rf(mapthis)
rf <- pull.rf(mapthis)
lod <- pull.rf(mapthis, what="lod")
lg <- formLinkageGroups(mapthis, max.rf=0.2, min.lod=10)

However, what's produced is one linkage group with >2000 markers, a second with ~50, and then hundreds of singlets. This issue remains mostly the same when I've tested various combinations of max.rf and min.lod (including the full dataset, even more so). I'm unsure of how to proceed with this or how to determine if it is a problem with my data. Any help is appreciated. Data is attached.

Thanks,
Alex R.

messages.author: 04e62c3b36bb17bf
messages.subject: Re: Linkage map construction with BC data
parts:
Hi Alex,
There are a number of potential causes for this. 
Have a look at your recombination fractions and the lod/rf relationship:

`plotRF(mapthis)`
`plot(as.numeric(rf), as.numeric(lod), xlab="Recombination fraction", ylab="LOD score", pch = ".")`

One possibility is that there are a bunch of markers that are out of phase. These diagnostic plots will tell you about that. You can also reference Dr. Broman's tutorial - http://www.rqtl.org/tutorials/geneticmaps.pdf.

It is also possible that your marker-binning is causing issues. You might consider pruning your genotype matrix by LD (e.g. SNPRelate::snpgdsLDpruning) instead of collapsing within scaffolds. 

Hopefully this helps,
John

Hi Alex,

I experienced this thing. Which generation of backcrossing are you? Most of the algorithms for linkage map construction are design for f2, bc1 and ril because more simple. If you are more advanced in generation you will get one LG with all the markers. Look also for segregation distorsion
